materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure expands the scope of FICC financing activities. In 2024, secured lending was described generally as 'structured credit and asset-backed lending, including warehouse loans...'. In 2025, it is refined to 'secured lending... through structured mortgage and other asset-backed lending' and significantly expands 'other FICC financing' to explicitly include 'facilitating institutional primary loans for syndication and providing structured letters of credit to corporate clients.' This adds new, specific business activities (syndication facilitation, letters of credit) to the disclosed risk and revenue profile.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company operates through four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), Global Banking, and Global Markets, with remaining operations recorded in All Other.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose their global investment banking and markets operations as distinct business segments. GS reports 'Global Banking & Markets' and specifically details 'FICC financing' activities such as structured credit, asset-backed lending, resale agreements, and commodity financing. Similarly, BAC reports 'Global Banking' and 'Global Markets' as separate segments, indicating a comparable structural approach to managing capital markets and investment banking businesses, though GS explicitly itemizes the financing products within FICC.

sentences.text: • FICC financing. Includes (i) secured lending to our clients through structured credit and asset-backed lending, including warehouse loans backed by mortgages (including residential and commercial mortgage loans), corporate loans and consumer loans (including auto loans and private student loans), (ii) financing through securities purchased under agreements to resell (resale agreements) and (iii) commodity financing to clients through structured transactions.

Through our various bank and nonbank subsidiaries throughout the U.S. and in international markets, we provide a diversified range of banking and nonbank financial services and products through four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), Global Banking and Global Markets, with the remaining operations recorded in All Other.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup is managed via five operating segments (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth, U.S. Personal Banking) with unassigned activities in All Other; International is further organized into six clusters for additional financial information, though not managed by the CODM.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi disclose their global markets and banking operations through distinct business segments. GS reports 'Global Banking & Markets,' specifically detailing FICC financing activities like structured credit and resale agreements. Citi reports 'Markets' and 'Banking' as two of its five operating segments. While GS integrates financing activities within the Markets segment description, Citi separates Markets and Banking into distinct reportable segments, yet both structure their global investment banking and capital markets businesses into dedicated segments distinct from consumer or wealth management units.

comparisons.peer_summary: Effective in Q2 2024, JPMorganChase combined its former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking segments to form the Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB), resulting in three reportable segments: Consumer & Community Banking (CCB), CIB, and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), with remaining activities in Corporate.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan disclose their capital markets and investment banking operations as key business segments. GS combines Global Banking and Markets, with specific mention of FICC financing (structured credit, asset-backed lending, resale agreements). JPMorgan reorganized in 2024 to combine Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking into a single 'Commercial & Investment Bank' (CIB) segment. While GS separates FICC financing activities within its Markets description, JPM consolidates banking and investment bank activities into one reportable segment, reflecting a different structural aggregation of similar commercial and investment banking functions.

sentences.text: • FICC financing. Effective in the second quarter of 2024, JPMorganChase reorganized its reportable business segments by combining the former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking business segments to form one reportable segment, the Commercial & Investment Bank.

As a result of the reorganization, the Firm has three reportable business segments - Consumer & Community Banking ("CCB"), Commercial & Investment Bank ("CIB") and Asset & Wealth Management ("AWM") - with the remaining activities in Corporate.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company's competitive position is affected by its ability to access capital at competitive rates and deploy capital efficiently, particularly in capital-intensive Institutional Securities activities, and by client demand for loans or lending commitments.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS highlight the capital-intensive nature of their institutional securities and financing activities. GS describes FICC financing as including secured lending, asset-backed lending, and commodity financing, which are inherently capital-intensive. MS explicitly states that its competitive position is affected by its ability to deploy capital efficiently in 'capital-intensive' Institutional Securities businesses, specifically mentioning 'financing and market-making activities.' Both disclosures underscore the significance of financing and capital deployment in their institutional securities segments, with GS providing specific product examples (structured credit, resale agreements) and MS focusing on the capital access and deployment constraints.

sentences.text: • FICC financing. Includes (i) secured lending to our clients through structured credit and asset-backed lending, including warehouse loans backed by mortgages (including residential and commercial mortgage loans), corporate loans and consumer loans (including auto loans and private student loans), (ii) financing through securities purchased under agreements to resell (resale agreements) and (iii) commodity financing to clients through structured transactions.

Our ability to access capital at competitive rates (which is generally impacted by, among other things, our credit spreads and ratings) and to commit and deploy capital efficiently, particularly in our more capital-intensive businesses within our Institutional Securities business segment, including underwriting and sales, financing and market-making activities, also affects our competitive position.
We expect clients to continue to request that we provide loans or lending commitments in connection with certain investment banking activities.
